catalog_quote: STRUCTURAL ELEMENTS. Two important phenomena are considered to be structural elements rather than segmental elements. ... The two important structural elements are "tone" and "doubling" ... Tone is here defined as the distribution of vocal tension over the syllable. Since its domain is fixed, i.e. the syllable, and since this domain is necessarily greater than a single segment in at least some cases, then tone is considered as an element of the structure rather than of any segment. ... Therefore, this part of the syllable, which is the syllable peak in Hockett's terms, is regarded as the tone-bearing segment. Every nucleus must bear a tone, of which there are four contrastive possibilities in the Ekoid Bantu Languages. These ... possibilities are: 1. High: a level of relatively greatest vocal tension; 2. new_statements.rule_in_words: Efutop (Crabb's Language M), like all Ekoid lects in the monograph, is described as a tone language: every syllable nucleus carries one of four contrastive tones (High, Low, Falling, Rising; a fifth/mid tone is posited only for languages N, O, P, T, U, i.e. not for Efutop). No statement about word stress or accent placement was found; probes of the indexed text returned no occurrence of the word 'stress'. Blench's Ekoid overview (held by the project, p. 6) likewise gives 'High, Low, Rising, Falling and Downstep tones' for Ekoid as a whole and says nothing about stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Tonally: mid tone added for languages N, O, P, T, U only.)
new_statements.domain_note: Crabb's statement is generic for the 14 Ekoid lects of the monograph, with the syllable as the tone domain; it is not an Efutop-specific prosodic description. Evidence is snippet-level (archive.org full-text search of a borrow-only scan); the book itself was not opened, so absence of a stress remark elsewhere in it cannot be fully guaranteed.
new_statements.identity_note: Crabb 1965 treats Efutop as 'Language M' of his minor sub-group M-P (Efutop, Nde, Nselle, Nta), vocabulary from Abaragba (consultant Anthony A. Eyam, per Wikipedia citing Crabb); the SIL 2008 audio wordlist is from Alesi village. Both are Efutop proper = efut1242 (ISO ofu). The only first-hand explicit no-stress statement held by the project is for a sister language, Western Ejagham (Watters 1981, ejag1239), and must not be transferred to Efutop.
